nodes.text: Shift ~168 ppm indicates carbonyl group; shifts 120-130 ppm indicate aromatic carbons; shift at 58.70 ppm suggests carbon attached to electronegative atom

support.quote: The presence of shifts around 168 ppm suggests a carbonyl group, while shifts in the range of 120-130 ppm indicate aromatic carbons. The shift at 58.70 ppm could indicate a carbon attached to an electronegative atom, such as an oxygen in an ether or alcohol.

nodes.text: Proton NMR: doublet 1.43 (3H), singlet 2.69 (6H), quartet 5.05 (1H), aromatic signals 7.13-7.90 ppm

Doublet at 1.43 ppm and quartet at 5.05 ppm (J=6.8 Hz) suggest an ethyl/methine group; singlet at 2.69 ppm (6H) suggests two equivalent methyl groups; aromatic signals suggest monosubstituted benzene ring

support.quote: The presence of a doublet at 1.43 ppm and a quartet at 5.05 ppm with a coupling constant of 6.8 Hz suggests an ethyl group. The singlet at 2.69 ppm indicates the presence of methyl groups, likely attached to a carbon that does not have any hydrogens (such as a quaternary carbon or a carbonyl carbon). The aromatic region (7.13 to 7.90 ppm) suggests a monosubstituted benzene ring.
